newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Vice-premier Li Lanqing urges greater ethnic unity in the northwestern region of Xinjiang.
- Economic tsar Zhu Rongji urges tighter rules to rectify the financial order and cut down on risks and says bad bank loans should be reduced by 2.0 percent annually over the next few years.

- The People's Bank of China issues notice saying that the principal on domestic debt of the failed China Agribusiness Development Trust and Investment Corp would be repaid by the China Construction Bank. Interest will not be paid.
- An official of the China Insurance Association recommends that several large foreign insurers be allowed to enter the Chinese market.
- The Beijing branch of the Ping'an Insurance Co forecasts premium income from life insurance to hit 1.5 billion yuan in 1997.
- People's Liberation Army delegates to the National People's Congress say China should boost development of defence technology and weaponry.
- Capital Iron and Steel Group plans to export 600,000 tonnes of steel in 1997, a rise of 11 percent from last year.
- A commentary slams New York Times for writing anti-China articles and seeking to split Tibet and Taiwan from the motherland.
- Fujian province sets up a port association to try to improve port management.
